subject: The (?^flags:...) qr wrapper is mishandled two ways: /xx loses an x, and qr/$re/ double-wraps (re/qr-72922.t)
description:
DONE s322 (34cbd2f). re/qr-72922.t 12/2 -> 14/0 OK.

The two diagnosed defects were real but neither was the cause. ROOT: the VarAnnotator froze the qr VARIABLE to its string form (B-regime raw-slot verdict; all uses "stringy" = interpolation + regex interpolation), so the object was already text before any regex saw it. Three fixes:
 1. Pl/VarAnnotator.pm: `write-object` reason — a root write whose RHS is a PPI::Token::QuoteLike::Regexp is never liftable by the B regime.
 2. p-regex-from-parts: returns the object itself when the pattern IS one interpolated regex (perl's rule), merging only the MATCH-time flags /g /c /e /r from the outer modifier string.
 3. p-regex-match gains a `source` slot (perl-side text); to-string prints (?^flags:SOURCE) and /xx prints both x's.

TRAP FOR THE FUTURE (cost one gate run): /g /c /e /r are flags of the MATCH OPERATION, not the compiled pattern. The first version returned the qr verbatim and `while ($t =~ /$re/g)` became an infinite loop (heap exhaustion) — Pl/t/regex-gpos-01.t t6.

Guard: Pl/t/transpile-test-09.t case 3, 15 rows incl. inverse guards. Spec: docs/ir-spec.md §10 regex rows; index line in DECIDED.md.
